hypothesis_version: v1 - final hypothesis wording (positive, significant, net of costs and market return)
asset_universe: US IPOs, SPACs excluded via old SIC-primary logic
data_and_features: Massive IPO endpoint + daily aggregates + SPY benchmark
model_or_rule: Mean day1-close to day2-close return (raw, market-adjusted, CS-cost-adjusted, flat-cost-adjusted); one-sample t-test + Wilcoxon signed-rank test vs zero
main_result: raw -0.15% (n.s., t_p=0.92, w_p=0.55); market-adj -0.16% (n.s.); CS-adj -3.82% (SIGNIFICANT NEGATIVE, t_p=0.023, w_p=0.0005); flat-adj -0.66% (n.s.)
reason: Established the pipeline end-to-end and gave the first read: hypothesis not supported at this stage. Used as an independent consistency check against the larger sample later.

asset_universe: Same as EXP-001, excluding the two most extreme observations (VTIX, SWMR)
model_or_rule: Same tests, re-run with the two largest outliers removed
key_parameters: Manual exclusion of 2 tickers, chosen as the largest |raw_return| in the sample
main_result: CS-adj mean moved from -3.82% to -4.14%, remained significant
reason: Confirms EXP-001's result was not driven by a couple of extreme observations - a deliberate robustness check before trusting the finding.

asset_universe: US IPOs 2020-2026, SPACs excluded via OLD (pre-fix) SIC-primary logic, NO price filter
data_and_features: Same endpoints as EXP-001, larger pull
key_parameters: No price filter applied at this stage
main_result: raw +1.11% (t_p=0.61 n.s. vs w_p<0.0001 SIGNIFICANT - stark disagreement between tests); market-adj +1.01% (same disagreement pattern); CS-adj -4.07% (t_p=0.065, w_p<0.0001); flat-adj +0.51% (t_p=0.81, w_p<0.0001)
reason: The sharp t-test/Wilcoxon disagreement was investigated and traced to ~24% of observations having economically implausible day-1 prices (reverse-split-distorted 'adjusted' prices on micro-cap names). Superseded by EXP-004 once this was fixed.

asset_universe: US IPOs 2020-2026, SPACs excluded via OLD (pre-fix) SIC-primary logic, price-plausibility filtered
data_and_features: Same as EXP-003 + a $3-$500 day1_close plausibility filter
key_parameters: Price band $3-$500, chosen from prior knowledge of typical major-exchange IPO pricing, not fit to the outcome data
main_result: raw -0.21% (t_p=0.70 n.s., w_p=0.045 weak sig); market-adj -0.30% (t_p=0.57 n.s., w_p=0.010 weak sig); CS-adj -4.29% (t_p<0.0001, w_p<0.0001, SIGNIFICANT); flat-adj -0.80% (t_p=0.13 n.s., w_p<0.0001 sig)
reason: t-test and Wilcoxon converge to a coherent story after removing implausible-price rows. Became the headline reported result, though flagged with the SPAC-classification limitation noted in EXP-007.

asset_universe: Same as EXP-004, restricted to listing_date < 2022-01-01
model_or_rule: Same tests, run on the pre-2022 subset only
key_parameters: Split date 2022-01-01, chosen to align with the well-documented IPO market downturn, not fit to data
reason: Robustness check: during the 2020-2021 IPO boom, raw/market-adjusted returns show essentially no effect (win rate ~49%, near coin-flip).

asset_universe: Same as EXP-004, restricted to listing_date >= 2022-01-01
model_or_rule: Same tests, run on the post-2022 subset only
main_result: raw -0.89% (t_p=0.32 n.s., w_p=0.0032 weak sig); market-adj -0.93% (t_p=0.29 n.s., w_p=0.0016 weak sig); CS-adj -5.21% (SIGNIFICANT, t_p<0.0001, w_p<0.0001); flat-adj -1.43% (t_p=0.11 n.s., w_p<0.0001 sig)
reason: Robustness check: post-2022, a small negative tilt emerges in raw/market-adjusted returns (detectable only by the distribution-robust test). CS-adjusted result significant in BOTH regimes - the most stable finding across the whole project.

data_and_features: cs_spread_estimate column vs a flat 0.5% assumption
model_or_rule: Direct arithmetic decomposition: mean(market_adjusted_return) - mean(cs_spread_estimate) compared against mean(net_abnormal_return); significance compared across the two cost measures
key_parameters: CS estimator (data-driven, per-ticker) vs flat 0.5% (fixed, outcome-independent)
main_result: Mean CS spread (3.67% initial sample, 3.99% extended filtered sample) almost exactly explains the gap between market-adjusted and CS-net-abnormal means in both samples; flat-cost measure shows consistently weaker/less stable significance
reason: Central interpretive finding of the whole project: the 'significant negative' CS-adjusted result is substantially a cost-estimation artifact rather than a large genuine reversal effect. Directly shaped the final conclusion's wording.

hypothesis_version: N/A - data pipeline / classification experiment, not a hypothesis test
asset_universe: 14 SIC-vs-heuristic disagreement cases from a fresh pipeline run
data_and_features: SIC code, issuer name, final_issue_price, ticker suffix, from Massive's IPO and ticker reference endpoints
model_or_rule: Old logic (SIC-6770 overrides heuristic when available) vs New logic (SIC-6770 OR heuristic, heuristic now includes ticker suffix 'U')

main_result: Old logic: 28.6% accuracy on the 14 known cases (missed 10/10 true SPACs). New logic: 85.7% accuracy (2 remaining errors: Newsmax and AIRO, real companies that coincidentally priced at exactly $10)
retained: Yes (logic); Not retroactively applied to EXP-003/004/005a/005b
reason: New classification logic adopted for all future runs. NOT re-run against the already-reported 2020-2026 results due to time constraints before the deadline - documented as an explicit limitation instead of silently left uncorrected. Highest-priority item in Next Steps.
